concepts.why: Uses int correctly as a whole-number loop index but says nothing more about int.

Treats length as the last valid index (everyday 'length 10 means item 10'), contradicting the rule that the last element is a[a.length-1]; this accesses data2[data2.length] and throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.

concepts.quote: for (int i = 0; i <= data2.length; i++) copy[i] = data2[i];
concepts.why: The for header syntax (init; condition; update) and body are well formed; the loop mechanics themselves are not misstated, only the bound borrowed from length_field is wrong.
Shows the element-by-element copying idea but never creates the new array (copy is undeclared) and overruns the bounds, so the new code is not a correct copy and cannot be L4.
